title: Dunga, Before Light
description: Oduya painted this from the shore at Dunga, the fishing beach outside Kisumu where she grew up watching the boats go out before dawn. The lake is a single band of cold silver under a violet sky, and one boat sits on the horizon like a mark of punctuation. The surface is built from thin, scraped layers, so the colours underneath come up through the grey like light through water.
condition: Very good. Light rubbing to the tacking edges from an earlier frame. No retouching under ultraviolet light.
provenance: Acquired from the artist by the present owner, Nairobi, 2022.
exhibited: Nairobi, Umber House, Lake: New Paintings by Achieng Oduya, March 2022.

title: Standing Figure (Ember)
description: Carved from a single cypress trunk felled near Eldoret, then charred and brushed back by hand until the grain shows silver through the black. At a little over head height, the figure narrows to a cut where a face might be, and leans very slightly forward.
condition: Very good. Fine natural checks in the wood, as made. The charred surface is stable and sealed.
provenance: Acquired from the artist, 2023; private collection, Nairobi.

title: The Blue Room
description: A woman in a marigold dress sits with her back to us in a sitting room painted entirely in cobalt: walls, curtains and the patterned cloth on the sofa are all the same intense blue, divided only by pattern. Painted in the first months of 2020, it is one of the largest of Nalubega's interiors.
condition: Very good. Unvarnished, as the artist intended.
provenance: Private collection, Kampala; by descent to the present owner.

title: Msasani, Last Bus
description: An empty bus shelter on the Msasani road after the last bus has gone, lit by a single sodium lamp. Mrema builds the orange light in thin glazes over a ground of deep teal, so the shelter glows while the road around it falls away into the dark.
provenance: Acquired from the artist by the present owner, 2024.

title: Field Notes IV
description: Some four hundred small rectangles, ruled by hand and painted in earth red, indigo and bone, cover the canvas edge to edge. Each was sealed with wax, scraped back and repainted several times, and the earlier layers show through at the edges of every cell. One of the larger works in the series, and the first of the square format.
condition: Very good. The wax surface has a soft, even bloom, as is usual for the series.
provenance: Private collection, Addis Ababa; acquired from the above by the present owner, 2019.
literature: Y. Gebremeskel, Field Notes 2009–2019, Addis Ababa, 2020, illustrated.

title: Head of a Listener
medium: Bronze with brown patina, on a hardwood base
description: The second head in Wekesa's Listener series: a long, smooth face with closed eyes, turned very slightly to one side as if catching a sound. The patina was built up over several weeks from a dark chocolate brown at the crown to a warmer bronze at the cheek.
provenance: Acquired from the artist, 2015; private collection, Nairobi.

title: Red Soil Hymn
medium: Soil pigment, charcoal and acrylic medium on raw canvas
description: A great arc of red earth sweeps up from the lower left of the canvas and breaks against bars of charcoal. Musyoka worked the soil, sieved from her family's land near Machakos, into the raw cotton with her palms and rags, and the marks of her hands are everywhere in it.
condition: Very good. A little loose pigment at the lower edge, stable.
provenance: Acquired from the artist by the present owner, 2022.

title: Fishermen Mending Nets
description: Four fishermen sit on an upturned boat at the Kivukoni fish market, mending a net that runs across the whole width of the picture. Mwakalinga breaks the figures, the boat and the shade of the market roof into flat, tilting planes of green and terracotta, and the net ties them together. One of the finest pictures of his market years, unseen in public since 1990.
condition: Good. A short, stable craquelure in the upper left sky. Small retouching at the lower right corner, visible under ultraviolet light.
provenance: Acquired from the artist by a British engineer working in Dar es Salaam, 1988; by descent to the present owner.
exhibited: Dar es Salaam, Paintings of the Harbour, a group exhibition, 1990.

title: Rusinga, Afternoon Rain
description: Rain moving across the lake towards Rusinga Island in the late afternoon, painted as a grey-green veil drawn down over bands of ochre and slate. Oduya scraped the rain into the wet paint with the edge of a board.
provenance: Acquired from the artist by the present owner, 2023.

title: Waiting, Entebbe Road
description: Two women wait on a bench in a pharmacy on the Entebbe road, under a wall of rose-pink tiles. Their dresses, one green and one striped, are painted as flatly as the tiles, so that the whole room becomes one woven surface.
provenance: Acquired from the artist, 2022; private collection, Nairobi.

title: Pair (Ash and Ember)
dimensions_note: Taller part 150 × 28 × 26 cm; shorter part 128 × 26 × 24 cm
description: Two standing forms carved from the same trunk, one burnt deeper than the other, so that one is a soft grey and the other a dense, shining black. Langat shows them close together, a hand's width apart.
provenance: Acquired from the artist by the present owner, 2024.

title: Kariakoo, Late Afternoon
description: Kariakoo market at the end of the day, when the shadows of the stalls stretch across the street and the crowd thins to a few figures carrying baskets home. A late picture of the market, with the planes of shade laid on in long, flat bands.
condition: Good. The board is sound and flat. Minor frame abrasion along the upper edge.
provenance: Private collection, Dar es Salaam; acquired from the above by the present owner, 2008.

title: Matatu, Ngong Road
medium: Linocut printed in black and red on paper
description: A matatu packed to the doors on the Ngong road, with passengers hanging from the back step and a conductor leaning out to shout the fare. Thuo printed the red, the matatu's painted stripe, from a second block.
condition: Good. Light toning to the sheet, margins intact.
provenance: Acquired from the artist, Nairobi, circa 1980; by descent to the present owner.

title: Water Tanks, Eastleigh
description: Black and blue plastic water tanks crowd a rooftop in Eastleigh, with a line of washing and the next roof beyond. Painted on the roof itself in an afternoon, in pale, open washes, with much of the paper left bare.
provenance: Acquired from the artist by the present owner, 2024.

title: Hills After Rain, Nyamagabe
description: Terraced hills fold one behind another into the distance, with mist lifting off the valley floor after an afternoon storm. Printed by the artist in his darkroom in Kigali.
condition: Excellent. Signed and numbered by the artist on the reverse.
provenance: Acquired from the artist by the present owner, 2020.

title: Doorway, Lamu II
description: A carved doorway in Lamu's old town, drawn in brown ink with a dip pen: the frame, the chains of carved flowers and the step worn hollow in the middle. The shade inside the half-open door is built from thousands of fine lines.
provenance: Acquired from the artist, Mombasa, 2022.

title: Study for Fishermen
description: A study for the painting Fishermen Mending Nets, offered as lot 8 in our live sale. Two of the four fishermen are here, drawn quickly with the side of the charcoal, and the net is already the line that holds the picture together.
condition: Good. Some smudging at the edges, as is usual with charcoal. Pin holes at the corners.
provenance: The artist's studio; acquired from the artist's family, 2021.

title: Mama Rehema, Kariakoo
description: A spice trader stands in front of the turquoise wall of her stall in Kariakoo, hands folded, in a headscarf the colour of turmeric. Kileo photographs every sitter in the place they work and lets them decide how to stand.
provenance: Acquired from the artist by the present owner, 2023.

title: Night Reeds
description: Papyrus reeds stand against the black water of the Nile at Jinja, with the outline of a moored boat behind. The blacks are wiped by hand, plate by plate, until they look like velvet.
provenance: Acquired from the artist, Jinja, 2017.

title: Mkeka (Saffron)
medium: Screenprint in three colours on paper
description: The interlocking chevrons of a woven palm mat, enlarged until each strand is as wide as a hand, printed in saffron, black and a sea turquoise.
provenance: Acquired from the artist by the present owner, 2021.

title: Brise-soleil, Noon
description: The concrete sun-screen of an office block photographed at midday, when the shadows of its fins fall straight down and the facade becomes a pattern of white and near-black.
provenance: Acquired from the artist by the present owner, 2022.

title: Lake Study 14
description: One of the small studies Oduya paints on the shore at Kisumu, to take back to the studio: three bands of grey, green and pale gold, and the line of the far shore.
provenance: Acquired from the artist by the present owner, 2021.

title: Market Day, Gikomba
medium: Linocut printed in black on paper
description: The second-hand clothes market at Gikomba on a Saturday, a crowd of shoppers and sellers pressed between stalls hung with shirts. Every figure is cut with the same quick, confident line.
condition: Good. A small repaired tear in the lower margin, well clear of the image.
provenance: Private collection, Nairobi.

title: Terraces, Morning
description: Early light picks out the edges of terraced fields on a hillside, each terrace a thin bright line above a band of shadow.
condition: Excellent. Signed and numbered by the artist on the reverse.
provenance: Acquired from the artist by the present owner, 2021.

title: Baraza bench
description: A long, low bench with a thick cypress seat resting on two blackened steel frames, the joints left visible at each end. Made to order for a house in Karen, and offered by its first owner.
condition: Very good. Light wear to the seat consistent with use.
provenance: Commissioned from the makers, 2022.

title: Tall bottle
description: A tall bottle with a narrow neck, fired for three days in Juma's wood kiln near Kilifi. Ash from the firing settled on the shoulder and ran down one side as a pale green glaze; the other side is bare, flashed orange by the flame.
provenance: Acquired from the artist by the present owner, 2023.

title: Kikapu pendant lamp
description: A wide pendant shade woven in natural sisal on a brass frame, with a brass ceiling cup and braided cable. Lit, the weave throws a soft pattern on the ceiling.
condition: Excellent. Rewired by the makers; supplied with a 1.5 m cable.
provenance: Acquired from the makers, 2024.

title: Lounge chair
description: A low lounge chair with a sloping cane back and seat in a slender teak frame, its arms ending in flat, rounded paddles. One of a group made for a guest house in Muthaiga and kept together until 2019.
condition: Good. The cane has been rewoven. Some fading to the teak.
provenance: A guest house, Muthaiga; private collection, Nairobi.

title: Long Rains
description: A large wall hanging in bands of colour that change slowly from top to bottom, from the slate grey of a rain sky to the deep green of the season after. The wool was dyed with indigo and leaves from Rashid's own garden.
condition: Excellent. Fitted with a hanging sleeve and batten.
provenance: Acquired from the artist by the present owner, 2021.

title: Kokwet low table
description: A low table cut from wild olive, with a thick top that follows the edge of the tree on one side and three short, tapered legs.
condition: Very good. A few fine surface marks to the top.
provenance: Acquired from the makers, 2020; private collection, Nairobi.

title: Coffee pot
description: A tall brass coffee pot with a long, beaked spout and a domed lid, the body hammered and chased with bands of leaves. Probably made in Mombasa.
condition: Good. Old dents to the body, wear to the tinning inside, as expected.
provenance: A family in Mombasa; private collection, Nairobi.

title: Pair of bowls
description: Two wide, shallow bowls fired side by side in the same kiln, so that the ash fell on each from the same direction: one carries a pool of green glaze at its centre, the other a ring of it around the rim.
provenance: Acquired from the artist, 2024.

title: Sideboard
description: A long, low sideboard in mahogany on a recessed plinth, with four sliding doors and slim brass handles set into the edges. Made for the offices of a coffee company in the Industrial Area.
condition: Good. Refinished. Minor marks to the top.
provenance: Offices in Nairobi's Industrial Area; private collection, Nairobi.

title: Mnara floor lamp
description: A tall, slender floor lamp with a blackened steel stem on a round brass base and a drum shade in undyed linen.
provenance: Acquired from the makers, 2023.

title: Upanga, 2 a.m.
description: A petrol station on an empty Upanga road at two in the morning, its forecourt a pool of orange light under the teal night.
provenance: Acquired from the artist.

title: Two Sisters, Kololo
description: Two sisters sit side by side on a patterned sofa in a house in Kololo, one in emerald and one in rose, against a wall of yellow lattice.
provenance: Private collection, Kampala.

title: Standing Figure (Charcoal)
description: An early standing figure, burnt to a soft charcoal grey and left rough at the base.
provenance: Acquired from the artist.

title: Field Notes II
description: An early square Field Notes, its grid weighted towards indigo, with a single band of red cells running across the lower third.
provenance: Private collection, Nairobi.

title: Kendu Bay, Noon
description: The lake at noon, when the light flattens everything: a pale gold sky, a white band of glare and a strip of blue-green water.
provenance: Acquired from the artist.

title: Head of a Sleeper
description: A head lying on its side, eyes closed, its patina running from green at the temple to brown at the jaw.
provenance: Private collection, Nairobi.

title: Market Women, Mwenge
description: Cloth sellers at Mwenge sit among bolts of fabric, their figures broken into planes of green, terracotta and white.
provenance: Private collection, London.

title: Dry Season Psalm
medium: Soil pigment and charcoal on raw canvas
description: Pale red earth dragged across the canvas in long horizontal strokes, broken by a single black vertical.
provenance: Acquired from the artist.

title: Kigamboni Ferry, Night
description: The ferry ramp at Kigamboni after the last crossing, its lamps doubled in the black water of the channel. A record price for the artist at auction.
provenance: Private collection, Dar es Salaam.

title: Listener II
description: A later Listener head, longer and narrower than the first, tilted back as if hearing something above.
provenance: Acquired from the artist.

title: Afternoon, Ntinda
description: A woman reads in a chair by a window in Ntinda, the curtains, the chair and her dress all printed with the same marigold flower.
provenance: Private collection, Kampala.

title: Field Notes VI
description: A Field Notes in which the bone-white cells crowd out the colour, leaving islands of red and indigo.
provenance: Private collection, Addis Ababa.

title: Kokwet lounge chair
description: A low cypress lounge chair with a slung saddle-leather seat and back, the frame joined with exposed through-tenons.
provenance: Acquired from the makers.

title: Large vessel
description: A broad, round-shouldered vessel, its surface flashed orange and grey, with a heavy fall of ash glaze on one shoulder.
provenance: Acquired from the artist.

title: Dry Season
description: A wall hanging that moves from straw yellow at the top to a dusty red at the bottom.
provenance: Acquired from the artist.

title: Pair of armchairs
description: A pair of open armchairs with splayed mahogany legs and seats and backs of tightly woven sisal cord.
condition: Good. The sisal has been rewoven.
provenance: Private collection, Nairobi.

title: Taa table lamp
description: A brass table lamp with a short, tapered stem and a woven sisal shade.
provenance: Acquired from the makers.

title: Writing desk
description: A teak writing desk with a bank of three drawers on the right and tapered legs.
condition: Fair. Water marks to the top.
provenance: Private collection, Nairobi.

title: Carved door panel
description: A single panel from a house door, carved in shallow relief with a running chain of flowers and a lotus at the base.
condition: Fair. Weathered, with old insect damage, stabilised.
provenance: A house in Mombasa's old town; private collection, Nairobi.

title: Set of three stools
description: Three round three-legged stools in cypress, each seat carved slightly hollow.
provenance: Acquired from the makers.
